scope: R198: pivot to the video VAE parallel goal and establish that its internal roofline is missing
why: the DiT decisions are all waiting on the user, while the objective lists encoder, video VAE and A2/A3 as parallel goals that are not blocked by those decisions

established_by_r138.tile_grid: 4x7 = 28 tiles over 8 ranks, 4 serial per rank
established_by_r138.conclusion: only the decoder internals can be changed to get under 20 s; the pipeline side has no room

excluded_by_r139.verdict: no speedup within noise, cold start +195 s, rejected
excluded_by_r139.inference: the bottleneck is not kernel launch count

the_gap: only total time and reproducibility were measured; there is no per-stage or per-layer breakdown of the 21.7 s, which is exactly the per-region roofline the objective asks for

primary_suspicion.observation: _VideoVAEPartProxy plus residency stagers mean VAE parts are shuttled between CPU and NPU, and the FP32 parameters are about 10.4 GB, which reconciles with the 13.436 GiB peak
primary_suspicion.hypothesis: if each of the 4 tiles re-shuttles the same parts, that is pure overhead and could be fixed without touching the maths
primary_suspicion.status: inference from code structure, not measured

next_steps: instrument decode_base with NPU Event timers per stage: up-block, conv, attention, upsample, then run one warm decode
measure _load_part_to_device and _offload_part_to_cpu call counts and total time, to see whether the same parts are re-shuttled per tile
use the breakdown to decide whether this is compute-bound (needs faster kernels) or shuttling/scheduling bound (possibly pure engineering gain)
cost_estimate: one run is about 240 s engine init plus 21.7 s decode, so roughly five minutes
limits: no new measurement this round, only code location and receipt consolidation
the re-shuttling hypothesis comes from code structure and is unmeasured
the agreement between 13.4 GiB peak and 10.4 GB FP32 parameters is arithmetic consistency, not proof
